reasons: Claimed status is compliant and, consistently, no redline or comment was proposed — the rendered paragraphs are byte-identical to the originals, so there is no invalid or directionally wrong edit to correct.

The cited grant (§ 4(c), p0021) supports the classification on the rule's material terms: it is royalty-free, non-exclusive and expressly 'perpetual', with no 'revocable' language and no discretionary revocation hook; the termination provisions (p0032, p0033) address the Agreement/SOWs, not revocation of the licence, so the walk-away scenario is absent.

The affiliates/contractors deterministic check fails only because the word 'Affiliates' is absent; the express 'right to grant a sublicense' coupled with the broad 'in connection with Company's business operations' purpose is a workable path to extend coverage to affiliates and contractors, which defeats the walk-away test ('excluded with no path to add them') and reaches the fallback in substance.
Successor transfer is addressed by p0042, where consent 'will not be unreasonably withheld', giving a practical M&A route — at the fallback rather than preferred.

Shortfalls versus preferred wording (no express 'irrevocable', affiliates/contractors not named, no explicit M&A carve-out) are correctly noted in the rationale as minor sub-elements rather than raised as deviations, in line with the playbook's classification semantics; flagging would have been over-flagging of an acceptable fallback clause.
